<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par64"/>but {{GHGheb|text=א}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע}} always have ''ē'' in 3rd ''sing''.—On the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with suffixes, cf. {{GHGpar|61|b}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|d}}
'''3.''' In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} being inadmissible in the middle radical, the preceding vowel, especially before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=ח}}, and {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, nevertheless, generally remains short, and the guttural is consequently to be regarded as, at least, ''virtually'' strengthened, cf. {{GHGpar|22|c}}; e.g. {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׂחַק}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִֽחֲלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּבִֽעַרְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִהַג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=13}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=אֵחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֵהַ֫לְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=13}}, but in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=יְנַהֵל}}, &c.; in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רֵעָה}}), {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=שַׂחֵק}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=רֻחַץ}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=דֹּחוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=36|verse=13}} from {{GHGheb|text=דָּחָה}}, also the unusual position of the tone in {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫חַן}}<ref>{{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫חַן}} is explained by Abulwalîd as the 3rd pers. {{GHGterm|perfect Puʿal}}, but by Qimḥi as a noun.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=18}}, and in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְרָחַ֫צְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=30}}); ''Hithpaʿēl perfect'' and {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הִטַּֽהֲרוּ}}, &c.; in {{GHGterm|pause}} (see {{GHGpar|22|c|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|27|q|nosign=1}}, {{GHGpar|29|v|nosign=1}}, {{GHGpar|54|k|nosign=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=הִטֶּהָֽרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=30|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְנֶחָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=19}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|e}}
The complete omission of the strengthening, and a consequent lengthening of the preceding vowel, occurs invariably only with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} ({{GHGheb|text=כָּרַּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}} is an exception; {{GHGheb|text=כֹּרָ֑תָה}} also occurs, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=28}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּרַךְ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּרֵךְ}}), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְבָרֵךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=בֹּרַךְ}}. Before {{GHGheb|text=א}} it occurs regularly in the stems {{GHGheb|text=בֵּאֵר}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּאֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵן}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֵּאֵר}}, and in the {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} of {{GHGheb|text=באשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=ראה}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שׁאה}}; on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=א}} is ''virtually'' strengthened in the ''perfects'', {{GHGheb|text=נִאֵף}} (once in the imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=23}}) ''to commit adultery'', {{GHGheb|text=נִאֵץ|translate=to despise}} (in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=17}}; according to Baer, but not ed. Mant., or Ginsb., even in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְנַאֵץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=10}}), {{GHGheb|text=נִאֵר|translate=to abhor}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=7}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נֵאַ֫רְתָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=40}}) and {{GHGheb|text=שִׁאֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=10}}; moreover, in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=יַאֵשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=20}}, according to the best reading. On the {{GHGterm|Mappîq}} in the {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=רֻאִ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=21}}, cf. {{GHGpar|14|d}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|f}}
Rem. 1. In the verb {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל|translate=to ask, to beg}}, some forms of the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} appear to be based upon a secondary form ''middle e'', which is {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} when the vowel of the {{GHGheb|text=א}} stands in an open syllable, cf. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵֽלְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵל֫וּנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=3}}; but in a closed syllable, even without a suffix, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֶלְתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאִלְתִּ֫יהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=20}}. Cf., however, similar cases of attenuation of an original ''ă'', {{GHGpar|69|s}}, and especially {{GHGpar|44|d}}. In the first three examples, if explained on that analogy, the ''ĭ'' attenuated from ''ă'' would have been lengthened to ''ē'' (before the tone); in the next three ''ĭ'' would have been modified to ''ĕ''. Also in the ''Hiphʿil''-form {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁאִלְתִּ֫יהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=28}} the {{GHGheb|text=אִ}} is merely attenuated from {{GHGheb|text=אַ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|g}}
2. In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} the lengthening of the vowel before the guttural causes the tone to be thrown back upon the penultima, and consequently the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} of the ultima to be shortened to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}. Thus (''a'') before monosyllables, according to {{GHGpar|29|e}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְשָׁ֫רֶת שָׁם|translate=to minister there}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=12}}, even in the case of a guttural which is ''virtually'' strengthened, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=18}} (see {{GHGpar|29|g}}). (''b'') after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיְבָ֫רֶךְ|translate=and he blessed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=22}} and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְגָ֫רֶשׁ|translate=and he drove out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתפָּ֫עֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=2|verse=1}}.
